region.text: Bactria and southern Transoxiana, the Kidarite kingdom on land of the Kushano-Sasanians

ledger.note: 360: a Kidarite kingdom takes Bactria. The page gives a decade, and 'firmly by 360'; the infobox dates the people to 320 and the end to 467.

360: the Kushano-Sasanians lose Bactria to the Kidarites. 'This administration continued until 360-370', 'when the Kushano-Sasanians lost much of their domains to the invading Kidarites'; the remainder went to the Sasanian Empire proper (infobox end c. 365). Year is the start of the page's range.

wars.name: Kidarite invasion of northwestern India
wars.outcome: The Kidarites took northern Afghanistan, then Peshawar and parts of Gandhara, and the Kushan remnants around Punjab.
wars.note: 'circa 390-410 CE'; the page adds that Gadahara coins may be the first Kidarite issues in the Kushan realm in India.

wars.name: Kidarite-Sasanian wars and tribute
wars.outcome: The Sasanians 'had lost many battles to the Kidarites' by Bahram IV (388-399) and paid them tribute under Yazdegerd I, Bahram V and/or Yazdegerd II; Yazdegerd II's refusal led to the war the Kidarites declared on Peroz about 464.
wars.note: No border moved on the page; the tribute runs against Cliopatria's allegiance of the Kidarites to the Sasanians (390-450).

wars.name: Kidarite-Gupta wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites may have fought the Guptas under Kumaragupta I (414-c. 455); Skandagupta repelled a Huna invasion in 455; the Kidarites seem to have kept western Gupta territory including Punjab until the Alchon Huns displaced them.
wars.note: The page hedges ('may have'); Skandagupta's Bhitari inscription speaks of Hunas, not Kidarites by name.

wars.name: Peroz I's war against the Kidarites

zones.text: the northern land added in 402, the Transoxiana and Syr Darya country of the Xionites' 387-401 shape; the Kidarites page puts their capital at Samarkand and the Hephthalites page has them lose 'Transoxianan lands' around 466

wars.outcome: The Kidarites declared war on Peroz about 464 after Yazdegerd II refused tribute; Peroz, allied with the Hephthalites, vanquished them in 466, held Tokharistan briefly and announced the victory at Constantinople in 467; the Kidarites withdrew to Gandhara and the south ('still controlled some places such as Gandhara and Punjab').
wars.note: The Hephthalites page dates their first defeat of the Kidarites to 450 and puts Transoxiana in their hands about 466.

certainty.note: A steppe-descended kingdom among Kushan and Sasanian successor states: no treaty line in the pages opened; the only treaty-like item (the 358 alliance of Shapur II with the Chionites) concerns the Xionites.

notes: Cliopatria shapes: 358 starts two years early (kingdom 360-370); the 443-450 shape drops the north 23 years before the Hephthalites page does (corrected to the 402 shape, plus new keyframes 451-465 and 466-467 ending in the south without Bactria: Gandhara and the Hindu Kush side); the row ends in 450 but the page ends the kingdom in 467 (infobox), with remnants in Gandhara and Kashmir that are not drawn. The 402-442 shape is the 390 shape plus the Xionites' shape and Cliopatria's White Huns row (410-450) is the Xionites' shape again, so two states hold the north in 410-442: the white-huns dossier (another part) should start the Hephthalites in the 440s (infobox 'Empire: 440s') or explain the overlap. The allegiance 'Kidarites to the Sasanian Empire' 390-450 (rel-allegiance-of-kidarites-to-sasanian-empire) is contradicted by the pages: the Sasanians paid tribute to the Kidarites. It is not drawn as a vassal tint of the Kidarites; whether the Sasanian side should carry a tributary tint is for the sasanian-empire dossier. Not settled: the start (the Kidarites page has the kingdom in 360-370, the Hephthalites page has the Kidarites 'who arrived from around 380 CE' and the Chionites 'circa 350 CE'; 360 follows the Kidarites and Kushano-Sasanian pages); the capital (Balkh by the infobox, Samarkand by the text); how the Xionite land passed to the Kidarites in 402; where the 450 defeat fell; the Kidarite remnants after 467 (Vinayaditya, the 477 embassy). The 'Little Kidarites' of Kabul and Beishi 'Daxia' records are not on the page read. States needing dossiers: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom (c. 230-365, slug kushano-sasanian-kingdom; sa-02 or me-06), Alchon Huns (alchon-huns; ia-01 or sa-02), Kushan remnants in Gandhara. No unknown gazetteer names. Budget: five pages of five (Xionites and Hephthalites shared with the xionites dossier). The Kidarites infobox gives 'Established: 320 CE' ('fl. 320: Kidara'); the start of 360 follows the text ('In 360-370 CE, a Kidarite kingdom was established'; Bactria held 'by 360'). (reviewer ia-01-b, 2026-10-18) Fix pass after review ia-01-b (2026-10-18): (1) Cliopatria's 387 shape adds about 0.22 M km2 in the south over the 358 shape (Kabul and the Hindu Kush side 0.18 M, Gandhara 0.04 M) with no event; the Kidarites page dates the conquest of the north-west of the Kushan world to 'circa 390-410', after 'consolidat[ing] their power in Northern Afghanistan', so the 387-389 keyframe is cut to the 358 shape's remainder and the addition is gained in 390 (Gandhara at confidence 2, the rest at confidence 1 against kushano-sasanian-kingdom, whose dossier is still needed). (2) The 466-467 keyframe and the 467 dissolve now hold the 390 shape without Bactria (about 0.27 M km2), not Gandhara alone, because the pages record the loss of Transoxiana and Bactria in 466 but not of Kabul or the Hindu Kush, and say the Kidarites 'still controlled some places such as Gandhara and Punjab'; no loss event to a third state is written for the Kabul side, as no page names a taker before the Alchon conquest of the last quarter of the 5th century. (3) Not settled: where Kabul and the Hindu Kush side stood between 466 and the Alchons (the Kidarites page does not mention Kabul, Kabulistan, Zabul or the Hindu Kush); the Kidarites page gives Punjab (central and western) to the Kidarites until the Alchon invasion, which Cliopatria's shape (73.6 E) does not reach.
